newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SocGen says considers Lithuania branch.
newsitem.headline: SocGen says considers Lithuania branch.

text.p: French banking group Societe Generale on Thursday confirmed that it was considering opening a branch in the Baltic state of Lithuania.

Denis Davidoff, SocGen area manager CIS and Baltic countries, told Reuters that he had met representatives of the Bank of Lithuania and that this was the beginning of its investigations of the market.
Societe Generale already has an office in the Latvian capital, Riga. The only other foreign bank with a branch in Lithuania is Poland's Kredyt Bank.
The central bank earlier said that central bank chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas met Davidoff to discuss setting up a branch this year.
"The French bank was interested in the situation in the Lithuanian financial market," a central bank spokeswoman said.
"The Societe Generale delegation and the Bank of Lithuania governor discussed the possibilities to open a branch office in Lithuania this year," the spokeswoman added.
She said that no concrete dates were set and that talks would continue in the future.
Lithuania was hit by a banking crisis at the end of 1995 which it spent the first half of last year recovering from.
However, analysts now say the sector is back on its feet with most banks reporting healthy 1996 profit rises.
Most of the leading banks in the northernmost Baltic state, Estonia, have also said they are considering expanding into Lithuania, the largest of the Baltic countries.
